site.title: Daniel Odin · Data Engineer
site.description: Daniel Odin is a data engineer in Gothenburg, Sweden, specialised in Scala, Spark and cloud platforms.

banner.alt: Daniel on a mountain top above beaches and fjords in Lofoten, Norway

about.lead: I'm a data engineer with a software engineer's mindset. I build data pipelines and platforms as maintainable code, made to run reliably in production.
paragraphs: For more than four years I worked on Apple Maps, starting with backend services and REST APIs in Scala. I then built and owned large-scale Spark and Flink pipelines, running daily with direct impact on production and the users of Apple Maps. Today I use that experience to help clients understand their data, turning raw data into intuitive reports in Microsoft Fabric and Azure.

A lifelong interest in mathematics and problem solving took me from mathematical statistics at the University of Gothenburg to an MSc in Computer Science at Chalmers, focusing on algorithms and machine learning.

I am curious, open-minded and eager to learn new things. Working on my own or in a group suits me well, but I prefer working in a team. I believe that working together is the best way to solve problems.

experience.summary: I work across the whole data chain for Xenit's clients: from pipelines in Microsoft Fabric, powered by Spark, to the Power BI reports at the end of the line. The goal is to make the clients' data useful, with automated reports.
highlights: Build data pipelines in Microsoft Fabric with Spark, Python and SQL.
Develop and automate Power BI reports.
Help clients make sense of their data.
experience.pdfSummary: Data pipelines in Microsoft Fabric (Spark) through to automated Power BI reports, helping clients make their data useful.

experience.summary: Part of a computer vision team working on digital inspection of railways, developing models that detect damage to the tracks. I built the pipelines and workflows that test and validate trained models before they are deployed to production.
experience.pdfSummary: Built pipelines and workflows that test and validate computer vision models for detecting railway damage before they are deployed to production.

experience.summary: I built and maintained large-scale pipelines in Spark and Flink for web-scraped data, and was responsible for several daily pipelines with high impact on production and end users.
highlights: Built solutions that load and transform data into Apache Iceberg.
Interviewed candidates in the recruitment process, especially for machine learning roles.

experience.summary: A feasibility study on forecasting brake squeal with deep learning, comparing forecasting techniques including the Transformer-based Informer architecture. The AFRY team built an end-to-end test framework that made it easy to compare models and run hyperparameter optimisation.
highlights: Analysed and forecast brake squeal time series.
Planned and presented results together with the client, including two presentations for around 100 people at Volvo Cars.
experience.pdfSummary: Forecast brake squeal with deep learning (incl. the Transformer-based Informer) in an end-to-end framework for comparing models and tuning hyperparameters.
pdfHighlights: Presented the results twice for around 100 people at Volvo Cars.

experience.summary: I worked in two teams: a large Scrum team validating large geospatial datasets, and a newly started web scraping team, where I built backend REST APIs for a scraping tool, using the GitHub APIs and PostgreSQL. I also supported other teams with web scraping.
highlights: Developed mostly in Scala (circe, http4s, cats, cats-effect), and also in TypeScript, Java and Python.

experience.summary: Camera-LiDAR Active Learning for Object Detecting Deep Neural Networks. Together with my thesis partner, we developed an algorithm that chooses which data a human should annotate (active learning) for 3D object detection, using ResNet-based deep learning models with LiDAR point clouds and camera images as input.
highlights: Presented the work at Chalmers and at Zenuity for 50–100 people.
experience.pdfSummary: Active learning for 3D object detection with camera and LiDAR data (ResNet-based deep learning).

experience.summary: I started as an R programmer writing scripts for figures and tables, worked as a statistician alongside my studies, and came back for a summer in 2019. I developed the R backend for the register's statistical visualisation, mostly a module that lets hip implant manufacturers follow market shares and outcomes for their implants.
highlights: Made all figures for the 2016 and 2017 annual reports and automated the process for the years after.
Helped other statisticians with programming and introduced new colleagues to the register's statistical environment.
experience.pdfSummary: Built the R backend for statistical visualisation of hip implant outcomes and automated the figures for the annual reports.
pdfHighlights: Co-authored five scientific papers in Acta Orthopaedica.
